blocks.x: Welcome to What’s On, our weekly roundup of notable shows. Here is what’s happening on TV from Sunday, September 20 to Saturday, September 26. All times are Eastern.

American Hostage (MGM+, Sunday, 9 p.m., series premiere) Based on the podcast of the same name, this 1970s-set true-crime thriller stars Jon Hamm as Fred Heckman, a beloved Indianapolis radio reporter who finds himself in the middle of a life-or-death crisis when hostage-taker Tony Kiritsis (Giovanni Ribisi) demands to be interviewed live on his radio program. The eight-episode story, which also stars Mireille Enos, Kristoffer Polaha, and William Jackson Harper, is just the first installment of a planned anthology exploring different real-life hostage crises in American history.

Youth (HBO and HBO Max, Sunday, 10 p.m., series premiere) Irish actress-writer Sharon Horgan (Catastrophe, Bad Sisters) continues her TV-comedy hot streak with this HBO romantic comedy. The multi-hyphenate stars as Alex, a London literary agent and 50-year-old divorcee who is navigating dating (she’s looking for “fun, lightly degrading sex”), and the existential dread of aging while caring for a pair of ailing parents (Brid Brennan and David Hargreaves) and a growing son (Aran Murphy, of Cillian stock). The cast also includes Sharlene Whyte, Rupert Friend, and Robbie Gee. Find The A.V. Club’s review on Sunday.

Line Of Fire (NBC, Monday, 10 p.m., series premiere) Peter Krause and Hope Davis lead this family-focused crime drama, which centers on the Hollingsworth clan, whose members work across various law-enforcement branches including the FBI, Secret Service, and the Department of Justice. (Thanksgiving at their house sounds like a blast.) After a standard case turns into a spiraling conspiracy, the gun-toting gang must use their expertise to protect one another and bring the perpetrator to justice, while trying not to kill each other in the process. Created by Josh Safran (Quantico, Gossip Girl), the NBC thriller also features Kat Cunning, Charlie Barnett, Campbell Scott, and Sam Waterston.

Brothers (Apple TV, Wednesday, series premiere) There are plenty of streaming shows based on a true story, but Apple TV’s newest comedy—starring Hollywood icons and real-life besties Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson as fictionalized versions of themselves—is instead pulled from a long-held rumor: that the uncanny resemblance and groovy je ne sais quoi that the actors share is actually the result of them secretly being half-siblings. (McConaughey’s mom allegedly knew Harrelson’s dad, if you catch our drift.) That premise is expanded in this eight-episode series, which sees the men’s lifelong friendship upended by the discovery of a decades-long family secret during an extended stay at McConaughey’s Texas ranch. Holland Taylor, Natalie Martinez, and Brittany Ishibashi co-star. The A.V. Club’s review drops on Wednesday.

A Different World (Netflix, Thursday, series premiere) A sequel series to the 1980s NBC sitcom of the same name, this Netflix revival follows Deborah Wayne (Maleah Joi Moon)—the rebellious youngest daughter of the original show’s Dwayne Wayne (Kadeem Hardison) and Whitley Gilbert (Jasmine Guy)—as she starts her freshman year at her parents’ HBCU alma mater, Hillman College. The 10-episode dramedy will mix Hillman newbies (Alijah Kai, Chibuikem Uche, Cornell Young IV) with A Different World O.G.s like Dawnn Lewis, Darryl M. Bell, and Cree Summer. (Original series director Debbie Allen is also back as executive producer and helms the reboot’s premiere.) Look out for The A.V. Club’s review on Thursday.
Also arriving
Best Medicine (FoX, Sunday, 8 p.m., season two premiere)
The Voice (NBC, Monday, 8 p.m., season 30 premiere)
Doc (FoX, Tuesday, 9 p.m., season three premiere)
Survivor (CBS, Wednesday, 8 p.m., season 51 premiere)
Toy Story 5 (Disney+, Wednesday, movie premiere)
American Horror Story (FX, Thursday, 9 p.m., season 13 premiere)
Jackass: Best And Last (Paramount+, Thursday, movie premiere)
The Great British Baking Show (Netflix, Friday, season 17 premiere)
Backrooms (HBO Max, Friday, movie premiere)
Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars (Apple TV, Friday, season two premiere)
Saturday Night Live (NBC, Saturday, 11:30 p.m., season 52 premiere)
Ending soon
Lioness (Paramount+, Sunday, season three finale)
America’s Got Talent (NBC, Wednesday, 9 p.m., season 21 finale)
Star Trek: Strange New Worlds (Paramount+, Thursday, season four finale)
Stuart Fails to Save the Universe (HBO Max, Thursday, 9 p.m., season one finale)
Fightland (Starz, Friday, 9 p.m., season one finale)
